stage1.impression: A clean, dark, warm render of two horn speakers in a fir-lined niche, but it reads as a CG home-theatre showroom, not a photographed room: the carpet, walls and tub chairs are smooth untextured surfaces, the fir boards look like a tiled wood map, the foreground Orb is a blown white disc, the projection on the left is the brightest broad surface, and the speakers sit as near-black silhouettes against a brighter wall with no tint or glow to make them the hero. None of the shell (concrete, beams, blackened steel) or the signs of life is visible, so a magazine would see a generic hi-fi demo room rather than a specific place.

blocking_9: The speakers must be the brightest, most legible thing in the frame: speaker region lum_median >= 45 with the smoke tint and white batts reading through the acrylic, not darker than the wall behind them (now 21 vs 90)
No hot spots on the niche: the altar spots' scallops on the fir clip 16 % of the band above the speakers; clip_pct < 1 there
The Orb's frosted liner must glow, not clip: clip_pct < 3 in its region (now 18.4 %)
The screen must sit below the speakers in brightness (now median 115)
At 1:1 the carpet, velvet, felt and fir need real texture: carpet pile, velvet sheen falloff, board grain variation and joints; no smooth CG surfaces

The frame must show what makes it this place: a fir beam, board-formed concrete or blackened steel at the edge of frame, and the props on the table (glass, record, sleeve against a plinth, coat on a chair) in view
Shadows hold detail: no large region more than half crushed (right chair now 50.8 %)
A trace of haze so the spots read as pools and the room has air

defects.what: Right speaker under-lit (lum_median 21.2), reads as a black box; smoke tint and white batts barely visible
Altar spots' scallops on the fir clip (clip_pct 16.0, median 174): the wall is lit, not the speakers
Orb lamp blown to a flat white disc (clip_pct 18.4, median 238); no frosted-liner gradation or tinted shell visible
Projection screen too bright (median 115), the largest bright area, competes with the speakers and reads as a flat CG plane
Carpet is a flat smooth surface, no pile or texture at 1:1; floor reads as a CG plane
Right tub chairs crushed (crush_pct 50.8) and blobby, smooth untextured velvet
Left chairs are dark smooth blobs, no velvet sheen
Fir boards look like a repeated, uniform wood texture with even vertical stripes; no checks, nail holes or board-to-board tone variation
Felt panels behind speakers are flat matte rectangles with crisp CG edges, no fibre
Light plinth glow reads as a white rectangle edge; the sleeve against the plinth reads as a flat grey card
Ceiling band nearly empty (median 3.6, crush 25.5 %): the fir beam is a dark slab, no shell visible
Frame clip_pct 1.06 % (above 0.5 % allowed outside lamps), largely from the niche scallops; no haze, air reads as vacuum

changes.problem: The speakers are darker than the wall behind them, so they read as black silhouettes instead of the tinted, lit hero.

change.setting: lamps on each speaker (4 x area, W/m2 at the target)
change.to: 1.5 W/m2, kept at 2900 K, placed to light the cabinet's acrylic and batts from inside/below so light passes through the smoke tint

changes.expected: Cabinets glow smoky brown-grey, batts read as soft white behind the acrylic, horn edges catch light; speaker median about 50-65.

changes.problem: The altar spots light the fir above the speakers into clipped scallops instead of lighting the speakers.

change.from: 70.0 W, cone 30 deg, aimed high on the wall
change.to: 35 W, cone 22 deg with soft blend, retargeted onto each speaker's horn and cabinet top (about z 1.1 m) so the pool falls on the speaker and spills down onto the plinth

changes.expected: No blown scallops; a pool of light on each speaker with the fir falling off naturally above; niche band median about 90-120.

changes.problem: The foreground Orb is a flat clipped white disc, the worst CG tell in the frame.

change.setting: each Orb's liner glow / Orb lamp
change.to: glow 0.03, 1.5 W (more light onto the table, less self-emission) and frosted acrylic roughness raised so the liner diffuses with a centre-to-edge gradient

changes.expected: The Orb reads as a smoked shell with a warm frosted core, bright but not blown, throwing a pool onto the oak table and the props.

changes.problem: The projection screen is the largest bright surface and pulls the eye away from the altar.
changes.expected: The screen sits as a dim cool-grey image at the edge of frame, below the speakers in brightness.

changes.problem: The frame shows a generic home-theatre room: none of the shell (concrete, fir beams, blackened steel) and none of the props are in view, and the eye-level 24 mm view reads as an architectural walkthrough.

evidence.measured: top band 0-120 median 3.6 with no readable beam; no glass, record or coat visible; no concrete or steel anywhere

change.to: seated height z 1.15 m, step back about 0.6 m and lens 32 mm so a fir beam crosses the top of frame and a slice of board-formed concrete or the blackened-steel edge of the zone shows at one side; frame the middle table with its glass and record in the near foreground, the coat over a tub chair at frame edge

changes.expected: The image reads as a specific room in a shell, seen from a seat, with signs of life leading to the altar.

changes.problem: Carpet, velvet chairs, felt and fir are smooth, uniform CG surfaces at 1:1.

evidence.measured: floor lum_range 87 over a large plane with no texture visible in crop; chairs smooth blobs; fir boards evenly striped

change.from: smooth carpet, plain velvet, uniform fir
change.to: carpet with a fine pile bump and slight colour noise; velvet with sheen (fresnel rim highlight) on the tub chairs; felt with fibre bump; fir boards with per-board tone variation of about +/-10 %, checks and a few nail holes, darker joints

changes.expected: At 1:1 each material reads at its real scale; chair silhouettes gain rim highlights that pull them out of black.

changes.problem: The High Contrast look crushes the near chairs and clips highlights at the same time, so the frame is both too dark and too hot.

change.to: AgX, look 'AgX - Base Contrast' (or Medium High Contrast), exposure 3.2 held, re-check after c1-c4

changes.expected: Shadows hold velvet and carpet detail, lamps stay bright but unclipped; frame median 30-45.

changes.problem: The air is a vacuum: the spots and the Orb make no pools in the air and the ceiling falls to black.
changes.expected: A faint glow around the altar spots and the Orb, a soft gradation into the ceiling, the beam readable.

out_of_scope.request: A more saturated or lighter speaker tint so the speaker is the frame's one colour
out_of_scope.why: The Smoke configuration's tint is fixed; the hero has to come from light through the acrylic (c1, c2), not a colour change.

out_of_scope.request: Stronger velvet or carpet colour, or removing the felt panels behind the speakers
out_of_scope.why: The zone's materials and layout are fixed by the room's design.

out_of_scope.request: Fewer or differently placed speakers (two identical copies read as repetition)
out_of_scope.why: The pair on the altar is fixed; it is a stereo pair, not a duplicated prop.
